title: Cykelslangen
description:
The Cycle Snake: a bikes-only ramp that winds above the harbourfront between Dybbølsbro and Bryggebroen, so riders skip the stairs. Opened in 2014, about 220 m long.

Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Bryggebroen
description:
Cycle and foot bridge between Islands Brygge and Vesterbro. Opened in 2006, about 190 m long.

Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Inderhavnsbroen
description:
Cycle and foot bridge between Nyhavn and Christianshavn. Its two halves slide apart to let ships through. Opened in 2016, about 180 m long.

Photo: European Commission, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Cirkelbroen
description:
Five circular platforms across the mouth of Christianshavn Canal, designed by Olafur Eliasson. Opened in 2015.

Photo: Karen Mardahl, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Lille Langebro
description:
Cycle and foot swing bridge beside Langebro, between the city centre and Christianshavn. Opened in 2019, about 175 m long.

Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Dronning Louises Bro
description:
The bridge across the Lakes between the city centre and Nørrebro, from 1887. Wide cycle tracks carry some of the heaviest bike traffic in the city.

Photo: Orf3us, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Åbuen
description:
Åbuen, the arch on the Nørrebro cycle route that takes riders over Ågade without a crossing. Opened in 2008, about 65 m long.

Photo: Leif Jørgensen, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Teglværksbroen
description:
Bridge across Teglværkshavnen in Sydhavnen, opened in 2011, with cycle paths on both sides.

Photo: News Oresund, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Knippelsbro
description:
Bascule road bridge from 1937 between the city centre and Christianshavn, with cycle lanes in both directions.

Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.

title: Langebro
description:
Bascule road bridge from 1954 between the city centre and Islands Brygge, with cycle lanes in both directions.

Photo: Sigfrid Lundberg from Lund, Sweden, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons. Location: OpenStreetMap contributors / Wikidata.
